full_text_en:
Guangdong Xingning Sanjian Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Xingning Municipal Bureau of Natural Resources, Guangdong Province — dispute over land administrative penalty

[Ruling Gist]

When imposing a penalty on historically leftover illegal land occupation without prior approval, the administrative authority shall fully consider the entire case circumstances, including the cause, process, time of the illegal land occupation, and the responsibilities of all parties. It shall adopt a law enforcement method that can both achieve the purpose of administrative management and protect the relative's legitimate reliance interests, while minimizing the impact on their rights and interests and social resource damage. The corresponding administrative penalty decision shall also comply with the principle of proportionality.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Judgment

(2021) Supreme People's Court Administrative Retrial No. 249

Petitioner (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Retrial Applicant): Guangdong Xingning Sanjian Engineering Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jinshui Loutai, Xingnan Avenue, Xingning City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Huanquan, General Manager.

Authorized Litigation Agents: Guo Junjie, employee of the company; Feng Hailong, lawyer of Beijing Zhongyin (Guangzhou) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance, Respondent): Xingning Municipal Bureau of Natural Resources, Guangdong Province. Domicile: Renmin Avenue, Xingning City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Weidong, Director.

Authorized Litigation Agents: Zhong Weichong, Deputy Director; Zeng Rongsong, lawyer of Guangdong Guangxing Law Firm.

The petitioner, Guangdong Xingning Sanjian Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanjian Company), dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 70 of the Meizhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province in a dispute over land administrative penalty against the respondent, Xingning Municipal Bureau of Natural Resources, Guangdong Province (formerly Xingning Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, hereinafter referred to as Xingning Resources Bureau), applied for retrial to the Guangdong High People's Court. After the Guangdong High People's Court dismissed Sanjian Company's retrial application by administrative ruling (2017) Yue Xing Shen No. 1232, Sanjian Company petitioned this Court. This Court, by administrative ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Xing Jian No. 1, granted the retrial and formed a collegial panel according to law, and heard this case in open court on April 19, 2023. Wang Huanquan, the legal representative of Sanjian Company, Guo Junjie and Feng Hailong, the authorized litigation agents of Sanjian Company, and Zhong Weichong and Zeng Rongsong, the authorized litigation agents of Xingning Resources Bureau, attended the hearing. This case is now concluded.

Facts found by the courts of first and second instance: On April 11, 2003, the Xingning Municipal Development and Planning Bureau submitted to the Meizhou Municipal Development and Planning Bureau the document Xing Ji Zi [2003] No. 14, "Request for Instructions on the Project of a Tea Art, Leisure, Entertainment and Sports Center," stating that Sanjian Company would raise funds to acquire 80 mu of land in Wuli Village, Fuxing Town to build a tea art, leisure, entertainment and sports center. The Meizhou Municipal Development and Planning Bureau approved the construction of the above project on April 28, 2003. On October 30, 2003, the Xingning Municipal Investment Attraction Office issued Xing Zhao Zi [2003] No. 22, "Reply on the Application for Land Use for the Project of Wulixiang Tea Art and Fitness Center," approving the site selection in the area of Wuli and Jinhua Villages, Fuxing Town, and agreeing that the land compensation fee (including resettlement compensation, seedling compensation, etc.) would be resolved at the price negotiated between Sanjian Company and Fuxing Town Government, and the land transfer price would be calculated based on the land acquisition cost minus the portion of fiscal revenue at the same level. On December 28, 2003, the Xingning Municipal Construction Bureau (now Xingning Municipal Bureau of Housing and Urban-Rural Development), in its Guangdong Province Construction Project Site Selection Opinion No. 04 Gui 001, also approved the site of Wulixiang Resort (including Wulixiang Tea Art Hall) in the section of Wuli Village and Jinhua Village, Fuxing Town, Xingning City, with a land scale of 110 mu. On September 18, 2003, Sanjian Company applied to the Xingning Municipal Construction Bureau for construction permit for the Wulixiang Resort Tea Art Hall. The application materials included a certificate issued by the Fuxing Land and Resources Office of Xingning Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources stating: "All land of Wulixiang Resort has been assisted in expropriation by our office. The land use certificate is being processed. Please handle the construction filing procedures for the relevant departments," and a letter of commitment from Sanjian Company promising to obtain as soon as possible the land use certificate, fire permit, etc., which were missing from the application materials. On February 12, 2004, the Xingning Municipal Construction Bureau issued Construction Project Planning Permit No. 04 Gui 006 approving the construction of the above building project, and on February 24 of the same year, issued Construction Project Construction Permit No. 441425200402240201 allowing the construction of Wulixiang Resort, with a construction scale of 4,036 square meters, located at the Fuxing Wuli section of National Highway 205 in Xingning City. Meanwhile, on February 10, 2004, the Xingning Municipal Construction Bureau issued Construction Land Planning Permit No. 04 Gui 001, allowing the procedures for the expropriation and allocation of land for Wulixiang Resort. In 2004, the Xingning Municipal People's Government (hereinafter referred to as Xingning Municipal Government), by document Xing Shi Fu Han [2004] No. 2, "Reply on the Request for Reduction or Exemption of Construction Filing Fees for Key Investment Attraction Projects" (hereinafter referred to as the "Reduction and Exemption Reply"), agreed to reduce or exempt relevant construction filing fees for projects including Wulixiang Resort.

Without obtaining the state-owned land use certificate for Wulixiang Resort, Sanjian Company began construction of the Wulixiang Resort Tea Art Hall in early 2004. On July 20, 2008, Sanjian Company entered into a "Wulixiang Site Use Contract" with Xingning Lidu Holiday Hotel (hereinafter referred to as Lidu Hotel), leasing part of the already constructed Wulixiang Resort Tea Art Hall buildings and site (area 3,000 square meters, including 2,000 square meters of building area and 1,000 square meters of open space) to Lidu Hotel for a contract term of 10 years (from August 1, 2008 to July 31, 2018), with a monthly site use fee of RMB 10,000.

On March 15, 2014, Xingning Resources Bureau began to investigate and handle the case of Sanjian Company's illegal land occupation and determined: Under the guise of investment attraction, Sanjian Company, without obtaining land use approval procedures, built the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall at the location of Liwu Gate, Huangchan Bridge, Wuli Village, Fuxing, adjacent to National Highway 205, occupying a total area of 10,216.67 square meters. In July 2008, Sanjian Company leased the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall to Lidu Hotel for decoration and operation until now. According to surveying, the main building of the completed hotel occupied 1,468.25 square meters, and upon verification, it conformed to the overall land use plan. On May 5 of the same year, Xingning Resources Bureau served by substituted service the "Notice of Hearing on Administrative Penalty for Land and Resources" on Wang Fopeng, the then legal representative of Sanjian Company, who was detained in Xingning Detention Center, and on May 6, directly served it on Wang Meiling, the authorized agent of Wang Fopeng. A hearing was held on May 27, in which Wang Meiling participated. The Report on the Administrative Penalty Hearing dated May 28 confirmed the facts verified by Xingning Resources Bureau. On May 29, Xingning Resources Bureau, on the grounds that Sanjian Company had occupied land to build the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall without obtaining land use approval procedures, issued to Sanjian Company the "Land and Resources Administrative Penalty Decision" (2014) Xing Guo Tu Zi Chu Zi No. 9 (hereinafter referred to as Penalty Decision No. 9): confiscation of the buildings and other facilities constructed on the illegally occupied 10,216.67 square meters of land. The above penalty decision was served by substituted service on Wang Fopeng, who was detained in Xingning Detention Center, on May 30, and on June 3, directly served on Wang Meiling and Lidu Hotel respectively. Dissatisfied with Penalty Decision No. 9, Sanjian Company filed an administrative lawsuit on August 25. The main reasons were: The land where the Wulixiang Resort was situated fell within the scope of Yue Guo Tu Zi (Jian) Zi [2009] No. 170, "Reply on the First Batch of Urban Construction Land for Xingning City in 2008," and was construction land, not agricultural land. Sanjian Company had paid the land lease payment for the disputed land to the Wuli Village Committee, Fuxing Subdistrict Office, Xingning City, for distribution to the villagers, of which 5 mu had undergone land expropriation procedures and the land transfer fee had been fully paid.

The administrative judgment (2014) Mei Xing Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 28 of the Xingning People's Court of Guangdong Province held: Pursuant to Article 43 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC (as amended in 2004) (hereinafter referred to as the Land Administration Law), which provides: "Any unit or individual that needs to use land for construction must apply to use state-owned land according to law," applying to use state-owned land is a necessary prerequisite for any unit or individual to carry out construction. In early 2004, under the guise of investment attraction and without obtaining land use approval procedures, Sanjian Company occupied land at the location of Liwu Gate, Huangchan Bridge, Wuli Village, Fuxing Subdistrict Office, adjacent to National Highway 205, to build the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall, covering an area of 10,216.67 square meters, and constructed on that land a tea art hall building covering 1,468.25 square meters and dormitory and shed buildings covering 706.93 square meters. Upon investigation, although the above actions of Sanjian Company conformed to the overall land use plan, these buildings were all constructed without applying to use state-owned land according to law. According to Article 46 of the Land Administration Law, which provides: "After land is expropriated by the state according to the statutory procedures, it shall be announced and organized for implementation by the local people's government at or above the county level," only the people's government at or above the county level has the power to expropriate land. With respect to the disputed land, the Xingning Municipal Government had not implemented any relevant expropriation actions up to the present time. Therefore, it could be determined that the certificate issued by the Fuxing Land and Resources Office regarding its assistance in expropriating the land was inconsistent with the facts, and the issuance of such a certificate clearly exceeded its statutory authority. The request for instructions from the Xingning Municipal Development and Planning Bureau, the reply from the Meizhou Municipal Development and Planning Bureau, the Construction Project Planning Permit, and the reply from the Xingning Municipal Government and other related evidentiary materials could not prove that Sanjian Company's construction activities on the disputed land had involved an application to use state-owned land according to law. Sanjian Company could not be exempted from the statutory obligation to apply to use state-owned land for its construction activities based on the above evidentiary materials. Hence, it could be proved that the fact that Sanjian Company had not applied for and obtained approval to use state-owned land for its construction on the disputed land was objectively present. Pursuant to Article 76 of the Land Administration Law, which provides: "Where land is illegally occupied without approval or by fraudulent means, the land administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order the return of the illegally occupied land; if agricultural land is converted into construction land in violation of the overall land use plan, the newly built buildings and other facilities on the illegally occupied land shall be demolished within a prescribed time limit and the land restored to its original condition; if it conforms to the overall land use plan, the newly built buildings and other facilities on the illegally occupied land shall be confiscated..." From the evidentiary materials provided by Xingning Resources Bureau, Sanjian Company's construction activities on the disputed land conformed to the overall land use plan of Xingning City. Therefore, Xingning Resources Bureau's action in confiscating the buildings and other facilities constructed on the illegally occupied 10,216.67 square meters of land against Sanjian Company complied with the above legal provisions.

At the same time, the fact that Sanjian Company illegally occupied the disputed agricultural land was confirmed by the criminal judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 34 of the Meizhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, which had taken effect. That judgment determined that Sanjian Company's act of constructing the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall in 2004 on land obtained from Wuli Village and Jinhua Village, Fuxing Subdistrict Office, without handling construction land use approval procedures, constituted the crime of illegal occupation of agricultural land. Therefore, the facts found and the law applied in Penalty Decision No. 9 were not improper.

Regarding the penalty procedure, Xingning Resources Bureau, when making Penalty Decision No. 9, strictly complied with the "Measures for Investigating and Handling Illegal Land Cases" and the "Provisions on Hearings for Land and Resources," and lawfully performed the procedures of acceptance, filing, investigation, holding a hearing, making a decision, service, and notification of remedies. Therefore, Sanjian Company's claim that the penalty procedure of Xingning Resources Bureau was illegal was not accepted.

In conclusion, Penalty Decision No. 9 had clear facts, was supported by sufficient and reliable evidence, and was procedurally lawful. Sanjian Company's lawsuit request to revoke the penalty decision clearly lacked factual and legal basis. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 56, paragraph (4) of the "Supreme People's Court's Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC," the court ruled: Dismiss Sanjian Company's claim to revoke Penalty Decision No. 9. Dissatisfied, Sanjian Company appealed.

The administrative judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 70 of the Meizhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province held: Article 43 and Article 44, paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law provide that any unit or individual that needs to use land for construction must apply to use state-owned land according to law; where construction occupies land involving the conversion of agricultural land into construction land, the approval procedures for the conversion of agricultural land shall be handled. The disputed land was collectively owned land of Wuli Village and Jinhua Village, Fuxing Subdistrict Office, Xingning City, with the use being agricultural land. Sanjian Company's act of building the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall on collective agricultural land without obtaining a state-owned land use certificate and without land use approval constituted illegal occupation of agricultural land. The above fact was confirmed by the effective criminal judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 34. Therefore, Xingning Resources Bureau's determination that Sanjian Company had illegally occupied land was clear in fact and supported by sufficient and reliable evidence. Although Xingning Resources Bureau had procedural flaws, they did not affect the characterization and penalty of Sanjian Company's illegal act, nor did they affect the exercise of Sanjian Company's rights. In summary, Penalty Decision No. 9 had clear facts, sufficient evidence, and complied with Article 76 of the Land Administration Law. Sanjian Company's claim to revoke the penalty decision lacked factual and legal basis. The first instance court's judgment to dismiss the claim was not improper and should be affirmed. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 61, paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the court ruled: Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. Dissatisfied, Sanjian Company applied for retrial.

The administrative ruling (2017) Yue Xing Shen No. 1232 of the Guangdong High People's Court held: Although Sanjian Company's construction activities on the disputed land conformed to the overall land use plan, they lacked land use approval procedures, violating Article 43 of the Land Administration Law. Xingning Resources Bureau, based on Article 76 of the Land Administration Law, made Penalty Decision No. 9, which was clear in fact and correct in law application. Sanjian Company's retrial application argued that when constructing the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall on the disputed land, it had obtained relevant documents such as the Construction Land Planning Permit and Construction Project Construction Permit, and thus the land use was lawful after approval by relevant government departments. However, land construction planning permit and land use permit are different types of administrative permits. Although Sanjian Company obtained the construction land planning permit, it did not obtain the land use approval procedures. Therefore, its claim that the land use act was lawful lacked legal basis and was not accepted. Sanjian Company's retrial application also argued that the criminal judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 34 had been revoked, there was no act of illegal occupation of agricultural land, the penalty procedure of Xingning Resources Bureau was illegal, and the use of the disputed land did not fall within the situation of lack of approval. It requested the revocation of the second instance judgment and a change of judgment in support of its claims. As these lacked factual and legal basis, they were not accepted. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 116, paragraph 2 of the "Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC," the court ruled: Dismiss Sanjian Company's retrial application. Still dissatisfied, Sanjian Company petitioned this Court.

Sanjian Company's petition argued: 1. The Wulixiang Resort Tea Art Hall was completed only after a series of decisions, permissions, approvals from relevant government departments and the efforts of Sanjian Company. Xingning Resources Bureau was also one of the approving and cooperating government departments. The issuance of Penalty Decision No. 9 by Xingning Resources Bureau constituted an abuse of power and should be revoked. 2. Based on the "Reply on the Land Use Application" dated October 30, 2003 from the Xingning Municipal Investment Attraction Office, Sanjian Company paid land acquisition compensation, seedling compensation, construction investment, and other amounts totaling RMB 39,833,934.97 according to the land acquisition cost standard negotiated with Fuxing Town Government. Moreover, the "Application Form for Supplementary Land Use Procedures" of the Xingning Municipal Government confirmed that Sanjian Company had paid all land acquisition compensation. 3. The criminal judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 34, which served as the basis for the first and second instance judgments, had been revoked upon retrial by the Zhongshan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, and the criminal retrial judgment was sufficient to overturn the determination by the first and second instance courts that Sanjian Company had illegally occupied agricultural land. 4. Xingning Resources Bureau imposed a relatively severe administrative penalty on Sanjian Company without collective discussion and decision, seriously violating statutory procedures. It requested: Revocation of the first and second instance judgments and Penalty Decision No. 9.

Xingning Resources Bureau responded: 1. Penalty Decision No. 9 had clear facts and conclusive evidence. When constructing the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall, Sanjian Company did not handle relevant lawful land use procedures, did not obtain relevant approval documents or land use certificates, and the land use was unlawful. 2. Penalty Decision No. 9 correctly applied the law. According to Articles 43 and 76 of the Land Administration Law, Sanjian Company did not lawfully handle land use procedures. Considering that Sanjian Company's buildings did not violate the overall land use plan, Xingning Resources Bureau's confiscation of the buildings and other facilities on the disputed land complied with legal provisions. 3. The procedure for Penalty Decision No. 9 was lawful. Xingning Resources Bureau, before making the decision, had performed the procedures of acceptance, filing, investigation, holding a hearing, making a decision, and notifying of remedies. 4. The document submitted by Sanjian Company, Yue Guo Tu Zi (Jian) Zi [2009] No. 170, "Reply on the First Batch of Urban Construction Land for Xingning City in 2008," did not involve the land for the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall project. The land for the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall, that is, the Lidu Hotel, did not obtain the land acquisition approval from the Guangdong Provincial Department of Land and Resources until 2017. Before 2017, it was agricultural land. It requested the affirmation of the second instance judgment.

Additional facts found by this Court upon retrial: The total land area of the Wulixiang Resort project was 107.2241 mu, consisting of three parts: the east side plot for the tea art and leisure center (approximately 84.7905 mu), the west side plot (approximately 9.2824 mu), and the disputed plot for the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall project (10,216.67 square meters, approximately 15.33 mu). Of the disputed approximately 15.33 mu of land, 10.2686 mu were leased by Sanjian Company in 2002 from villagers or villagers' groups of Wuli Village through the Fuxing Town Government and Wuli Village Committee under the pretext of building a flower nursery; 3.8362 mu were leased by Sanjian Company in 2002 from villagers of Jinhua Village through the Fuxing Town Government and Jinhua Village Committee under the pretext of building a flower nursery, later changed to a one-time "expropriation" at the standard of RMB 46,537 per mu due to dissatisfaction with annual rent payments; and the remaining approximately 1.23 mu were river embankment land.

Xingning City Bureau of Land and Resources issued the "Opinion on Land Use Pre-approval for the Tea Art Leisure and Entertainment Sports Center Project" on April 4, 2003, approving 80 mu (approx. 5.33 hectares) of land for the project, which conformed to the functions and layout of Xingning City's overall urban plan, and requiring Sanjian Company to promptly go through land use procedures with the bureau after project approval. The Xingning City Investment Promotion Office issued Xingzhao Letter [2004] No. 10, the "Letter on Reporting the Construction Start Progress of Key Investment Projects" (hereinafter referred to as Letter No. 10) to Sanjian Company on January 16, 2004, stating: Wulixiang Resort is a project eligible for the reduction or exemption of construction-related fees under Xingfa [2003] No. 6. It hoped that Sanjian Company would, upon receipt of the letter, earnestly formulate a construction schedule, complete the project construction as soon as possible, and strive for the development of the Xingning regional economy, and report the construction schedule and progress to the office on a monthly basis. On February 11, 2004, the Xingning City Government issued the "Approval for Reduction and Exemption of Fees," agreeing to reduce or exempt construction fees for Wulixiang Resort, including ten categories of administrative and other fees such as municipal construction supporting fees and project quality supervision fees, in order to implement preferential investment policies. On December 28, 2004, the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall project was rated as the 2004 Meizhou City Safe Production and Civilized Construction Excellent Model Site by the Meizhou City Construction Bureau.

After the completion of the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall in December 2004, the Xingning City Government reported to the higher authorities to complete the land use procedures on the grounds that the land for the Wulixiang Resort project was historically used land that had been occupied before approval. The Guangdong Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued Yue Guotu Zi (Li Yong) Letter [2004] No. 777, the "Reply on Improving the Procedures for Historical Land Use" (hereinafter referred to as Reply No. 777) on October 22, 2004, agreeing to improve the historical land use procedures for the Wulixiang Resort project, with the time and procedures to be handled in accordance with Yue Guotu Zi Dian [2004] No. 42. However, the Xingning City Government and its relevant functional departments only reported the land for the tea art leisure center (84.7905 mu, approx. 5.65 hectares) to complete the land use procedures. The Wulixiang Tea Art Hall project and the land to its west involved in this case have never had their land use procedures completed as required by Reply No. 777. On September 1, 2017, the Guangdong Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued Yue Guotu Zi (Jian) Zi [2017] No. 470, the "Reply on the First Batch of Urban Construction Land in Xingning City for 2017," approving the expropriation of 14.8185 mu (approx. 0.99 hectares) of the land involved in the case.

It was further found that after the Xingning City Resources Bureau confiscated the buildings and other facilities constructed by Sanjian Company on the land involved in the case through the No. 9 Penalty Decision on May 29, 2014, the Xingning City Government held an executive meeting on June 24, 2015, deciding to demolish the buildings and other facilities on the land due to, among other reasons, safety hazards. Subsequently, the Xingning City Bureau of Land and Resources entrusted a third party to carry out the demolition. The land involved in the case is currently idle.

It was also found that between July and August 2015, in order to resolve the issue of refunding the land costs and earth-filling costs already paid by Sanjian Company, a series of written correspondence took place among Sanjian Company, the Fuxing Subdistrict Office, the Xingning City Resources Bureau, and the Xingning City Land Reserve and Land Acquisition Service Center. On August 25, the Xingning City Resources Bureau and the Xingning City Land Reserve and Land Acquisition Service Center submitted a "Request for Approval to Refund Land Compensation and Earth-filling Costs Related to Certain Plots to Sanjian Company" to the Xingning City Government, stating that the total costs amounted to 8.77 million yuan (including 3.7 million yuan in land compensation, 3.2 million yuan in interest for the same period, 950,000 yuan in earth-filling costs, 890,000 yuan in attachments such as retaining walls, and 21,000 yuan in rent for the holiday hotel land advanced by the subdistrict office). Later, for various reasons, the above costs were not actually refunded to Sanjian Company's account. On December 24, 2018, the Xingning City Resources Bureau issued the "Explanation of the Situation Concerning the Land Involved in the Case of Sanjian Company," stating that according to the calculations of the Fuxing Subdistrict Office, Sanjian Company and its affiliated enterprises had paid a total of 3.15 million yuan in land compensation and other costs for the tea art leisure center plot, the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall plot, and the plot to its west, of which 2.75 million yuan was for the tea art leisure center plot.

During the retrial of this court, we organized conciliation efforts between the parties regarding remedial measures and compensation, but the conciliation was unsuccessful.

Opinion of the Court: Article 43, Paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law (revised in 2004) stipulates that any unit or individual that needs to use land for construction must apply for the use of state-owned land in accordance with the law, except for the establishment of township enterprises and the construction of residential houses by villagers with the approval to use land collectively owned by farmers of that collective economic organization, or for the construction of township (town) village public facilities and public welfare undertakings with the approval to use land collectively owned by farmers. Article 76, Paragraph 1 stipulates that anyone who illegally occupies land without approval or by deception, or by fraudulent means, shall be ordered by the land administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level to return the illegally occupied land; if the land conforms to the overall land use plan, the buildings and other facilities newly constructed on the illegally occupied land shall be confiscated, and a fine may also be imposed. In this case, Sanjian Company, the Xingning City Government, the Xingning City Resources Bureau, the Xingning City Construction Bureau, and others all knew that the construction of the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall required the application for use of state-owned land in accordance with the law. The administrative organs such as the Xingning City Government and the Xingning City Resources Bureau, as well as the owners of the collective land involved in the case, all agreed to Sanjian Company's use of the land involved, had already collected corresponding fees, and had processed the corresponding approval procedures for the expropriation and conversion of agricultural land for the collective land involved in the case for state-owned construction land. However, at the time the No. 9 Penalty Decision was made, the land involved in the case had still not fully completed the approval procedures for the expropriation of collective land and the conversion of agricultural land, nor had it completed the legal state-owned land transfer procedures. Therefore, Sanjian Company's construction of the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall in advance, while the land involved in the case was still collective agricultural land, was clearly illegal.

However, the legality of the penalized decision is also dependent on whether it violates the principle of proportionality between punishment and fault, and whether the penalty decision is commensurate with the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of the illegal land occupation. That is, when making the No. 9 Penalty Decision, the Xingning City Resources Bureau should have considered whether there were statutory mitigating or extenuating circumstances, whether there were other methods of handling that could eliminate the illegal state, and whether confiscating the buildings and other facilities already constructed on the land involved in the case required protecting Sanjian Company's reliance interest in the government's administrative actions.

First, although the project involved in the case did not go through the legal procedures for expropriation, conversion of agricultural land, and transfer, it had gone through a series of other construction approval and permit procedures. The illegal commencement of construction of the project involved in the case was carried out with the support and cooperation of local administrative organs. The series of construction approvals obtained by Sanjian Company, including the land use pre-approval opinion, project establishment approval, project land use approval, construction land planning permit, construction project planning permit, and construction project construction permit, all indicate that the Xingning City Government, the Xingning City Resources Bureau, the Xingning City Construction Bureau, and other administrative organs permitted the implementation of the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall project despite knowing that the land in question had not yet legally obtained approval for expropriation and conversion of agricultural land, nor had it been legally transferred to Sanjian Company. Letter No. 10 from the Xingning City Investment Promotion Office and the "Approval for Reduction and Exemption of Fees" from the Xingning City Government also required the project involved in the case to be completed as soon as possible and reduced or exempted various construction fees and charges. In particular, to assist Sanjian Company in applying for construction approvals, the Fuxing Land and Resources Office, affiliated with the Xingning City Resources Bureau, issued a certificate stating, "All the land for Wulixiang Resort has been expropriated with the assistance of our office. The land use certificate is being processed. Please give the relevant departments the approval for construction procedures." The above series of administrative actions indicate that the illegal actions of the Xingning City Government and related functional departments were one of the main reasons for the illegal occupation of the land involved in the case, and also an important reason why the problem of illegal land occupation was not resolved in a timely manner and persisted for over ten years.

Second, although the project involved in the case conformed to the local overall land plan and the former Guangdong Provincial Department of Land and Resources had agreed to complete the land use procedures, the long-term failure of the Xingning City Government and relevant departments to promptly complete the approval procedures was an important reason why the illegal land use state was not eliminated in a timely manner. It was precisely because of the awareness that the Wulixiang Resort project had problems of occupying land without prior approval and illegal construction that the Xingning City Government and relevant functional departments successively took a series of measures to complete and improve the land use procedures. Upon the application of the relevant departments in Xingning City, the Meizhou City Bureau of Land and Resources on March 25, 2004, listed the Wulixiang Resort project as a historically illegal land use project and applied to complete the procedures for the conversion of agricultural land and expropriation. On October 22, 2004, the Guangdong Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued Reply No. 777, agreeing to improve the historical land use procedures for the Wulixiang Resort project, including the project involved in the case, with the time and procedures to be handled in accordance with Yue Guotu Zi Dian [2004] No. 42. However, the Xingning City Government and its relevant departments only reported the land for the tea art leisure center (84.7905 mu) to the east of the land involved in the case to complete the land use procedures, but the land involved in the case had never had its land use procedures completed as required by Reply No. 777. The Xingning City Government and relevant departments clearly bore corresponding responsibility for Sanjian Company's failure to legally obtain the land use rights for the land involved in the case.

Third, Sanjian Company had already paid part of the land compensation and other costs for occupying the land involved in the case for construction. On October 30, 2003, the Xingning City Investment Promotion Office issued Xingzhao Zi [2003] No. 22, the "Reply on the Application for the Use of Land for the Wulixiang Tea Art and Fitness Center Project," approving the site selection for the project and agreeing that land compensation fees (including resettlement compensation, seedling compensation, etc.) would be resolved at the price negotiated between Sanjian Company and Fuxing Town Government, and that the land transfer price would be calculated based on the expropriation cost minus the local fiscal revenue portion. Although the above reply's requirement to pay land compensation fees and the method for determining the land transfer price did not comply with the procedural provisions of the Land Administration Law regarding land expropriation, compensation, and transfer, it was also an important reason why Sanjian Company illegally occupied the land and failed to pay all costs in accordance with the law. The "Explanation of the Situation Concerning the Land Involved in the Case of Sanjian Company" issued by the former Xingning City Bureau of Land and Resources on December 24, 2018, can prove that Sanjian Company and its affiliated enterprises paid a total of 400,000 yuan in compensation fees for the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall and the plot to its west (totaling 24.6124 mu, approx. 1.64 hectares). During the retrial court hearing, the Xingning City Resources Bureau also acknowledged that Sanjian Company had paid certain compensation fees for the land involved in the case.

Finally, the penalty imposed by the Xingning City Resources Bureau on Sanjian Company should be commensurate with the facts, subjective fault, and degree of harm of the violation, achieving proportionality between punishment and fault. Article 4, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the PRC (as amended in August 2009) in effect at the time stipulated: "The imposition of administrative penalties shall follow the principle of fairness and openness. The establishment and imposition of administrative penalties must be based on facts and be commensurate with the facts, nature, circumstances, and degree of social harm of the illegal act." The principle of proportionality between punishment and fault must be adhered to in administrative penalties. When an administrative organ applies an administrative penalty to a violator, the type and extent of the penalty imposed must be commensurate with factors such as the facts of the violation, the degree of fault, and the degree of social harm. In this case, Sanjian Company, as a real estate development and operation enterprise, knew that constructing the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall on the land involved in the case required obtaining relevant land use approval procedures. However, it still proceeded with the project construction by "expropriating" or leasing the cultivated land involved in the case through Fuxing Town Government under the guise of building a flower nursery, constituting illegal land occupation. Furthermore, during the ten-year period of using the land involved in the case, Sanjian Company still failed to urge the relevant government departments to complete the land expropriation and transfer procedures, and should bear corresponding legal responsibility. However, the Xingning City Government and relevant functional departments, despite knowing that Sanjian Company had not obtained legal land use procedures, still supported and assisted in the construction of the project involved in the case under the guise of investment attraction, failed to complete the project land use procedures as required by Reply No. 777, and acquiesced in Sanjian Company's method of leasing land instead of expropriating it for prior construction, and should also bear corresponding legal responsibility. Sanjian Company had formed sufficient reliance on the illegal administrative actions of the Xingning City Government and relevant functional departments, and the resulting reliance interest should also be protected in accordance with the law.

Therefore, when the Xingning City Resources Bureau made the No. 9 Penalty Decision in 2014, it should have fully considered the overall circumstances of the case, taking into account the reasons, process, time, and responsibilities of all parties for the illegal land occupation. Moreover, given that the land in question conformed to the overall land use plan and the provincial government had already agreed to complete the historical land use procedures for the Wulixiang Resort project, the enforcement method should have been one that could both achieve the purpose of administrative management and cause the least damage to the rights of the counterparty and social resources. The Xingning City Resources Bureau should have given priority to taking remedial measures for the historical illegal land occupation (such as building without prior approval), promptly completing the approval procedures for the expropriation and conversion of agricultural land for the land involved in the case in accordance with the law, and providing Sanjian Company with the opportunity to legally obtain land use rights through the bidding, auction, and listing process, so that the illegal land occupation could be legalized. Even if remedial measures could not be taken, the fault of Sanjian Company and the relevant government departments should have been comprehensively considered, and a fair and reasonable decision should have been made. However, nearly ten years after the Wulixiang Tea Art Hall was built and put into use, the Xingning City Resources Bureau summarily confiscated it and then had it demolished. This was clearly disproportionate to Sanjian Company's fault and the degree of social harm. The administrative penalty was manifestly unjust, wasting social resources, affecting the construction of a law-based government and a government of good faith, and infringing upon Sanjian Company's reliance interest. It should not be supported. Pursuant to Article 70, Item 6 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the No. 9 Penalty Decision should have been revoked. However, given that the buildings and other facilities on the land involved in the case have been demolished and cannot be restored to their original state, revocation of the No. 9 Penalty Decision has no practical significance. Therefore, pursuant to Article 74, Paragraph 2, Item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the No. 9 Penalty Decision should be confirmed as illegal. The judgments of the first and second instance courts, which respectively dismissed Sanjian Company's claims and appeal, were based on unclear facts and erroneous application of law, and should be corrected.

It should be noted that since Sanjian Company did not file a compensation claim at the time of filing the lawsuit, and although the parties had previously negotiated the refund of land costs and earth-filling costs paid by Sanjian Company, they did not negotiate remedial measures or compensation for the losses caused by the confiscation and compulsory demolition. Therefore, this court will not address the issue of remedial measures or compensation in this case according to law. However, after this judgment takes effect, the Xingning City Resources Bureau shall proactively negotiate specific remedial measures or compensation methods with Sanjian Company for the losses caused to Sanjian Company by the illegal actions. If negotiation fails, the Xingning City Resources Bureau shall determine the amount of loss in accordance with the law and, taking into account the degree of fault of both parties in the violation, promptly make a compensation decision. If Sanjian Company is dissatisfied with the compensation decision, it may file a separate lawsuit in accordance with the law.

In summary, the No. 9 Penalty Decision violated the principle of proportionality between punishment and fault and was manifestly unjust. The first and second instance judgments were based on unclear facts and erroneous application of law, and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 74, Paragraph 2, Item 1, and Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 119 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the Administrative Judgment (2014) Mei Zhong Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 70 of the Meizhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province and the Administrative Judgment (2014) Mei Xing Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 28 of the Xingning People's Court of Guangdong Province;

2. Confirm that the "Land and Resources Administrative Penalty Decision" (Xing Guo Tu Zi Chu Fa Zi [2014] No. 9) of the Xingning Natural Resources Bureau of Guangdong Province is illegal.

The first and second instance case acceptance fees of 100 yuan shall be borne by the Xingning Natural Resources Bureau of Guangdong Province.

This judgment is final.
